correctness.rationale: The dual Lipschitz ball of the four-point metric is exactly |v|,|w|<=s, 2|u|+|v|+|w|<=1. Symmetry averaging reduces all ellipsoids to Q=a u^2+v^2+w^2 without increasing distortion. Convex corner maximization gives M(a)=max(a/4,a(1-s)^2/4+s^2,a(1-2s)^2/4+2s^2). The exact boundary minimum is min(s^2,a/[2(a+2)]), by weighted Cauchy and feasible equality for a<=a0; if a>=a0 the Cauchy lower bound exceeds s^2. For a<=a0 the last maximum dominates, its ratio has strictly negative derivative; for a>=a0 all maximum branches are nondecreasing. Thus a0=4s^2/(1-2s^2) is globally optimal and R(a0)=2+(1-2s)^2/(1-2s^2). The result covers s in (0,1/2], treats limits properly, and an exact rational script checks 1800 instances.

originality.rationale: Targeted published-finding corpus semantic searches for two-cherry four-point ultrametrics, the dual three-coordinate Lipschitz polytope, ellipsoid distance, and the exact formula found no direct coverage. Closest inspected primary ultrametric/free-space theorems give structural L1 embeddings or qualitative isomorphisms rather than sharp Euclidean distortion. Two other related four-point Euclidean computations have genuinely different metrics (single exceptional edge; weighted four-cycle). The identification of an optimal quadratic form and a nonconstant sharp Hilbert-distance profile is not logically implied by any inspected result. Remaining possibility of equivalent historical convex-body formulation is explicitly acknowledged.
residual_risks: Equivalent old literature may use a convex-body polytope/ellipsoid rather than Lipschitz-free terminology; no exhaustive originality certification is possible.
Relevant sections of four identified primary papers were inspected; every unrelated section in the literature was not exhaustively read.
No extension to asymmetric ultrametrics, higher dimensions, non-real scalars or the coalesced t=0 metric is proved.

value.rationale: Balanced four-point ultrametrics are the smallest symmetric two-level finite ultrametrics and arise as a two-cherry dendrogram. Their free spaces form a canonical three-dimensional family. The result computes the exact optimal Euclidean structure and nontrivial sharp interpolation in distortion from sqrt(2) to limiting sqrt(3), refining qualitative l1-isomorphism results. The family is natural, every continuum parameter is covered, and the explicit quadratic form is reusable in geometric comparisons; no arbitrary numerical slice or known-table recomputation is needed.
